title: Billing & Compliance Gating for Cloud Listing
body:
Purpose:
This working doc standardizes the billing, privacy, and compliance acceptance checks required before approving a Redwood product listing across public cloud marketplaces (AWS Marketplace, Azure Marketplace, GCP Marketplace). It is intended for GTM ops, sales engineering, legal, and engineering owners to run a consistent preflight for partner and internal listings.

Context / Why this exists:
We frequently see friction during final approval cycles caused by gaps in billing sku mapping, trial provisioning behavior, and regional data residency locks. This causes last-minute engineering work and delayed launch dates. To reduce churn, this checklist ties required copy snippets, gating technical checks, and role owners to each acceptance criterion so launches can be greenlighted reliably.

How to use this doc (quick):
- Owner (GTM ops) shares the listing PR/asset bundle.
- Run the checklist sections A-D. Each item is a binary accept/fail with a short remediation note.
- If any A-level (billing/security) items fail, block the listing; escalate to SE and legal.
- If only B/C items fail, schedule a remediation sprint before publish and add a launch contingency.

A. Critical Billing & Contracting checks (blocker if not met)
1) SKU mapping and metering definition: SKU exists in our internal pricing catalog and maps to marketplace product sku (exact match). Include human-readable billing unit (token, request, seat).
   - Acceptance: SKU ID in product catalog submitted, example mapping provided.
   - Example copy snippet: "Unit: inference-tokens (billed per 1k tokens). Trial allowance: 10k tokens."
2) Trial provisioning behavior: Marketplace trial or free-tier triggers backend entitlement call and creates a tenant in Redwood with isolated trial quota.
   - Acceptance: End-to-end sanity test recorded (video or step list) and automated smoke test added to CI.
3) Entitlement and plan reconciliation: Marketplace metering reports can reconcile to customer's Redwood invoice; no double-billing risk.
   - Acceptance: Billing integration tested in staging with at least one sample invoice and reconciliation report attached.
4) Legal hooks & contract flow: Link to approved commercial terms (or Marketplace terms addendum) and verification that legal countersigned templates are attached.
   - Acceptance: Confluence legal-approved terms doc linked.
5) Refund / cancellation workflow: Clear documented flow for refunds or cancellations initiated via marketplace; support playbook updated.
   - Acceptance: Support playbook snippet present and tested with support staging account.

B. Security & Compliance gating (high priority)
1) Data residency and regional availability: Listing copy must declare data region(s) and whether customer data is processed in-region or replicated.
   - Acceptance: Data residency field populated; architecture diagram link present.
2) PII processing statements: If the listing cites PII processing or enterprise integrations (SaaS connectors), include minimal PII handling statement and relevant DPA clause reference.
   - Acceptance: DPA or privacy addendum linked; privacy team sign-off attached.
3) KMS and key management options: For Private/Dedicated offerings, listing must call out supported KMS/HSM integrations.
   - Acceptance: CLI config sample and KMS config doc linked.
4) SOC/ISO/other certifications: If product claims compliance (e.g., SOC2), include evidence location and expiration date.
   - Acceptance: Certification references in listing copy and Cert PDF linked.

C. Product experience & Copy checklist (non-blocker but high UX importance)
1) Hero blurb (25–40 words): A single sentence describing value and deployment modes. Provide 2 variants: developer-focused and enterprise-focused.
   - Developer variant: "Low-latency, cost-efficient LLM inference with flexible deployment: hosted API, reserved capacity, or private VPC."
   - Enterprise variant: "SLA-backed inference with private deployment and integrated observability for predictable production performance."
2) 3 key bullets (capabilities): latency, cost controls, rollout tooling. Keep each < 12 words.
3) Quickstarts & code snippet: Include a 3-line curl and SDK example (Node/Python) that works with trial entitlements.
4) Screenshots & telemetry examples: Per-route latency chart and cost-per-token table. Attach images with alt text and captions.

D. Ops readiness & automation checklist
1) Staging listing lifecycle: End-to-end smoke test exists for a staging listing flow that mirrors marketplace flows (provision -> meter -> reconcile -> revoke).
   - Acceptance: smoke-test log attached or CI job link.
2) Escalation matrix: Who to call for billing disputes, legal escalations, and P0 incidents.
   - Acceptance: PagerDuty group and email aliases listed.
3) Rollback policy: If marketplace reporting is incorrect or replication fails, the listing has an automatic soft-disable flag and rollback steps documented.
   - Acceptance: runbook snippet with commands and thresholds.
4) Monitoring and alerts: Marketplace metering ingestion must surface anomalies (sudden spike in reported units) and alert finance + SRE.

Acceptance rubric & signoff flow (recommended):
- Step 1: SE uploads listing draft -> GTM ops runs A-D red/green checklist.
- Step 2: If any A fails: block and assign to engineering/legal and schedule emergency fix.
- Step 3: If A passes but B/C fail: record remediation backlog item with target date; signoff contingent on remediation completion.
- Step 4: Final signoff: GTM lead, Finance lead, Legal lead, and Owner initial and date.

Copy bank (short snippets for listing assets)
- Short headline: "Predictable, production-grade LLM inference"
- Value tagline: "Reduce token costs with intelligent batching and cache-aware serving."
- CTA: "Start a free trial on [Marketplace] and get 10k tokens free."
- Legal alt CTA: "Contact sales for dedicated capacity and enterprise SLAs."

Example acceptance notes (fill with concrete items when running):
- SKU mapping: PR #143 added SKU-788 to pricing catalog; needs pricing tier confirmation from Finance (actioned).
- Trial provisioning: smoke-test-video.mp4 uploaded to PR; failing when customer email contains plus-sign, remediation in backlog.
- Data residency: EU-only flag verified; architecture diagram: /confluence/arch/rgw-prod-residency.

Open questions for next iteration:
- Should we mandate a minimum set of telemetry visuals for all public listings? (pros: reduces back-and-forth; cons: more design work pre-PR)
- For partner listings, do we require a sandbox metering account for partners to validate reconciliation?

Next steps / owner actions:
- GTM ops to run this checklist for current AWS & Azure drafts; collect missing artifacts by 2025-01-20.
- Legal to confirm DPA clause for marketplace flow and update Confluence link.
- SE to add CI smoke-test for trial provisioning edge-cases (due 2025-01-17).

Appendix: quick checklist summary (copy/paste to PR)
[ ] SKU mapping confirmed and sample invoice attached
[ ] Trial provisioning smoke test passed
[ ] Reconciliation test completed in staging
[ ] Legal terms linked and approved
[ ] Data residency statement present
[ ] KMS / encryption options documented
[ ] Hero blurb + 2 bullets added
[ ] Quickstart snippet included and validated with trial
[ ] Support playbook updated with refund/cancellation flow
[ ] Monitoring alerts configured for metering anomalies

Maintainer: GTM Ops (Jordan Kim)
Last review: 2025-01-12
